Class CredentialChangeService

java.lang.Object
grafiosch.service.CredentialChangeService
@Service public class CredentialChangeService extends Object
Atomic credential writes, session invalidation and notices, addressed by user id rather than the caller's tenant.

    • resetPassword

      @Transactional(isolation=READ_COMMITTED, rollbackFor=Exception.class) public Integer resetPassword(String token, String passwordNew) throws Exception
      Null means unknown, expired, spent or ineligible. A failed policy check leaves the token intact. TOTP, recovery codes and passkeys are not touched: a mailbox proof revokes bearer credentials only.
      Throws:
      Exception

      public void checkNotDemo(User user)

    • writePendingTotp

      @Transactional(isolation=READ_COMMITTED, rollbackFor=Exception.class) public void writePendingTotp(Integer idUser, String secretBase32)
      Starts or replaces a TOTP setup. Only the pending secret changes, so the sessions stay and no notice is sent.
      Parameters:
      idUser - the user
      secretBase32 - the new secret, shown to the user once

    • clearPendingTotp

      @Transactional(isolation=READ_COMMITTED, rollbackFor=Exception.class) public void clearPendingTotp(Integer idUser)
      Discards an expired setup; an enabled factor stays as it is.

    • enableTotp

      @Transactional(isolation=READ_COMMITTED, rollbackFor=Exception.class) public CredentialChangeService.RecoveryCodesChange enableTotp(Integer idUser, String verifiedPendingSecret, long confirmedStep)
      Makes the pending secret the active factor and replaces the recovery codes.
      Parameters:
      idUser - the user
      verifiedPendingSecret - the pending secret the code was verified against; when a setup started meanwhile in another window replaced it, nothing is enabled
      confirmedStep - time step of the confirming code, which is spent with the enrolment
      Returns:
      the new recovery codes and the authentication version after the change

    • renewRecoveryCodes

      @Transactional(isolation=READ_COMMITTED, rollbackFor=Exception.class) public CredentialChangeService.RecoveryCodesChange renewRecoveryCodes(Integer idUser)
      Replaces all recovery codes of a user with an enabled factor; the previous ones become invalid.

    • disableTotp

      @Transactional(isolation=READ_COMMITTED, rollbackFor=Exception.class) public int disableTotp(Integer idUser)
      Removes the authenticator-app factor and the recovery codes on the user's own request.
      Returns:
      the authentication version after the change

    • removeSecondFactorByAdmin

      @Transactional(isolation=READ_COMMITTED, rollbackFor=Exception.class) public void removeSecondFactorByAdmin(Integer idUser)
      Removes the second factor of another user on behalf of an administrator. Passkeys stay; the user's sessions end. The caller receives no token.

    • consumeRecoveryCode

      @Transactional(isolation=READ_COMMITTED, rollbackFor=Exception.class) public boolean consumeRecoveryCode(User user, String codeHash)
      Spends a recovery code and tells the user how many are left. The authentication version stays: spending a factor is no change to the set of credentials.
      Parameters:
      user - the user signing in or confirming an action
      codeHash - SHA-256 hash of the normalized code
      Returns:
      true when the code was valid and is spent now

    • addPasskey

      @Transactional(isolation=READ_COMMITTED, rollbackFor=Exception.class) public CredentialChangeService.PasskeyChange addPasskey(Integer idUser, Supplier<org.springframework.security.web.webauthn.api.CredentialRecord> register)
      Registers a passkey. Demo account, account status and the limits are checked again inside the transaction that inserts the row, under the lock of the user, so parallel completions cannot exceed UserPasskey.
      Parameters:
      idUser - the user
      register - verifies the credential and inserts it (registerCredential of the relying party)
      Returns:
      the new passkey and the authentication version for the replacement token

    • deletePasskey

      @Transactional(isolation=READ_COMMITTED, rollbackFor=Exception.class) public int deletePasskey(Integer idUser, Integer idUserPasskey)
      Deletes a passkey of the user. It removes access and leaves the password, so it needs no proof; it ends the other sessions and sends a notice.
      Returns:
      the authentication version after the change
